_help: What computers say when nobody has written them a file of their own, and the advisor's hints inside one. A board, console or panel in a room, or a door with a hack on it, gets a generic computer made from this and from what the world knows about the place. {place} is the place's name, {room} the room's, {holder} who holds the place, {person} and {other} two people from the place, {user} the login name. Hints are by training level, from untrained to master, each level adding its lines to the ones below; {unread} and {unreadMail} count what's not been opened, {programs} lists the programs, {trace} is the trace in percent, {left} the actions left before it completes, {network} the other computers reachable from here.

default: All sessions are monitored. Have a safe and productive shift.
This node hasn't been patched since the Fall. Nobody's left who knows how.
Reminder: the manifests are confidential. Sharing them is an offense.
Scheduled maintenance has been cancelled, due to the end of civilization.
yours: CFS Meridian. Nine hundred souls aboard a ship built for three hundred.
Welcome back, Captain. The night watch left the kettle on.
Every system on this board answers to the bridge, and the bridge answers to you.

console.desc: A terminal with a cracked bezel and a cursor that still blinks. Whoever used it last didn't log out.

programs.name: Post a notice
programs.text: You type a line onto the board that everyone here reads. It'll be there until someone takes it down.

programs.name: Wipe the day's log
programs.text: The day's entries go, one by one, and the counter at the bottom drops to zero. Somebody will notice the gap. -> * flag wiped_log_at_{place}: The day's log at {placeName} was wiped

server.desc: A rack with its door open, humming, warm as a kitchen. Every record of this place goes through it.

programs.name: Read the accounts
programs.text: Columns of what came in and what went out, and a column that doesn't add up, which somebody has initialled every week.

programs.name: Move a little of the float
programs.text: A rounding error in your favour, spread over forty entries. -> * credits 40: A rounding error on {placeName}'s books; * flag skimmed_{place}: You moved money off {placeName}'s books

panel.desc: A door panel: a keypad, a light, and a speaker grille that crackles when you touch it.

programs.name: Open the door
programs.text: The lock thinks about it, then lets go. -> * door here

programs.name: Read the lock's log
programs.text: Who's been through, and when. More names than you'd expect for a locked door.

power.desc: A power board: breakers in rows, half of them hand-labelled, one of them warm.

programs.name: Cut the lights
programs.text: The breaker goes over and the room drops to the emergency strips. -> * flag lights_cut_at_{place}: The lights were cut at {placeName}

programs.name: Bring the lights back
programs.text: The breaker goes back, and the hum returns. -> * unflag lights_cut_at_{place} ? flag lights_cut_at_{place}

manifest.name: manifest.txt
manifest.text: Stock on hand at {placeName}, by the day's count: {goods}.

roster.name: roster.txt
roster.text: On the books at {placeName}: {people}. {holder} signs for all of them.

accounts.name: accounts.ldg
accounts.text: Receipts, fees and the float. A column of initials down the right-hand side, the same initials every week.

access.name: access.log
access.text: Opened and closed, opened and closed. The last through: {person}, who didn't close it properly.

load.name: load.txt
load.text: Power draw by section, all of it over the line someone drew in red ten years ago.

notes: "Told the night shift the password. Do NOT write it down." Someone wrote it down.
Reminder: the coffee machine is not a network device.
If {person} asks, the shipment was late. If {other} asks, it was early.
Count the crates twice. The second count is the one that goes in the book.

mail.subject: The count
mail.text: The count's short again. I didn't write it down this time. Come and see me before you tell anyone.

mail.subject: Re: The count
mail.text: Don't put it in a message. Don't put anything in a message. We'll talk.

mail.subject: Manifests
mail.text: The manifests are confidential. Sharing them with the fleet, with the Ministry, or with anyone who asks nicely is an offense. You know who you are.

0: Reading is safe on most computers. Running a program is what the trace notices.
Each program says what it does before you run it.
1: {unread} files and {unreadMail} letters you haven't opened yet.
3: The trace is at {trace}%: about {left} more actions before it completes.
